name: Fingerprinting ban and ATT enforcement
plain: Apple forbids deriving a device identity from signals to track someone who said no under ATT.
meaning: Stops apps and SDKs from rebuilding an ID from IP, model, locale and similar signals after the person refused tracking. It is enforced mainly at App Review and by required reason API gating.

android.store_policy: Google Play Ads policy: use the advertising ID for ads; persistent IDs allowed only for non-ad uses with privacy policy
android.note: Play does not ban probabilistic matching or IP use; Google changed its ad products to allow IP address use in Feb 2025 and the UK ICO criticised the change.

ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.2(i): no device or user fingerprinting; ATT rules
ios.api_surface: Required reason APIs, privacy manifests, NSPrivacyTrackingDomains
ios.note: Apple states fingerprinting violates the rules even with consent banners. Enforcement is review rejection and, since 2024, required reason API reasons plus blocked tracking domains.

limits.headline: Can't rebuild your identity from phone details after you refuse tracking on iPhone
limits.user_action: Nothing. You said no on the tracking prompt; Apple enforces it in review
can: Use ordinary details for fraud and app function, within Apple's rules
Measure results in groups without naming you
Use IP addresses on Android; Play does not ban it
cannot: Combine IP, model and language to build an ID on iPhone
Hide it behind a consent banner
Use blocked tracking sites after you said no
Pass App Review if found doing it
limits.differs: Apple bans fingerprinting even with a banner. Google Play does not ban matching and now allows IP use in ads.

story.what_it_is: Apple's rule that bans rebuilding a device ID from small clues after you say no to tracking.

marketing.name: App Review Guidelines, Data use and sharing
marketing.pitch: Apps must not derive data from a device to identify a user who declined tracking.

story.for_you: You do not see anything. It is a rule that says: if you tap 'Ask App Not to Track', the app may not secretly follow you anyway using your phone model, language and IP address.
story.for_makers: Makers who use fingerprinting risk rejection. Apple enforces it at App Review and through required reason APIs, so ad networks moved to clearly permitted measures like SKAN.

use_cases.example: An ad network that mixed IP and model to rebuild an ID could see its apps pulled.
A game studio drops a probabilistic attribution tool to avoid a rejection.
A measurement firm limits itself to consented IDs and anonymous aggregates.
Fraud teams may use signals to stop abuse, but not to track people for ads.
A retailer is told to remove a script that built a device profile from signals.
A developer reads the guideline and rewrites its tracker to use only IDFV inside its own apps.

story.android_note: Android has no equal rule, but Google Play bans abusive fingerprinting for ads on kids apps.
story.ios_note: Applied mainly through App Review and the privacy manifest process.

technical_bounds: Review rejection for SDKs that fingerprint
NSPrivacyTrackingDomains blocked at the network layer when ATT is not granted (declared domains only)
Enforcement is largely review time, not runtime

history.change: Apple tells developers ATT cannot be bypassed by fingerprinting
Required reason APIs announced to curb signals used for fingerprinting
Required reason API reasons enforced for new uploads (1 May 2024)
